title: Cycle slot shepherd and staffing-derivative protocol
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: We lack a lightweight, repeatable mechanism for holding small capacity reserves in each product cycle that do not require reassigning feature owners but allow quick response to emergent platform incidents, hot customer requests, or critical reliability work. Current approaches either (a) over-commit engineers to conservative scope cuts that slow OKR progress, or (b) keep no reserves and require mission-critical context-switches that cause regressions and long recovery time.

Proposal summary: Introduce a 'cycle slot shepherd' protocol and a small set of staffing-derivative controls that together create an operational buffer without heavy process overhead. The protocol creates 1-2% of FTE-equivalent reserve per cycle as flexible "slots" owned by a cycle steward. Slots are consumed by defined event types (reliability incidents, enterprise security requests, regression hotfixes, prioritized pilot customer work) and are replenished or traded with teams via lightweight swap transactions.

Key components:
- Slot pool: canonical ledger tracking available slots for the cycle, owned by PM steward.
- Slot contracts: short form agreements listing acceptance criteria, expected impact window (1-3 days), and fallback owner.
- Shadow staffing: temporary shadow assignment pattern so a slot-consumer can borrow 0.25-2 engineer-days without reassigning feature ownership.
- Replenishment rules: if used, the originating team either (a) defers a non-blocking subtask, (b) accelerates the next-cycle handoff, or (c) draws from a cross-cycle credit line.
- Escalation & audit: all slot claims logged to a dashboard with reason, requestor, approver, and resolution time; P95 resolution target = 48h.

Why this matters: Keeps OKR momentum while allowing disciplined, traceable responses to unpredictable operational needs. Creates a predictable miniature market for scarce engineering time that product and eng leadership can observe and tune.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- A working slot ledger prototype exists in Confluence + a simple Airtable/Sheet by 2026-02-26.
- Cross-functional policy doc (PM/Eng/Design) reviewed and approved by product leadership by 2026-03-05.
- Pilot run with two squads during 2026-W11 showing: at most one slot claim per week, average claim time <= 36h, and no OKR churn > 8%.
- Dashboard metrics (slot inventory, claim reasons, resolution time, OKR drift) wired into a shared Grafana view for leadership by 2026-03-26.

Scope of work: policy definition; ledger UI (sheet); small dashboard; pilot coordination; retrospective and policy iteration. Not included: deep scheduling tool integrations or automated payroll adjustments.

Rollout plan: 1) Build policy + ledger; 2) Run 3-week pilot with two product areas (Console + Dedicated); 3) Evaluate pilot metrics and tuning thresholds; 4) Expand to all product cycles with handbook entry and automated template.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict reserve vs flexible slots: strict reserves protect feature velocity but waste idle time; flexible slots optimize utilization but require governance; we choose a lightweight flexible approach to minimize overhead.
- Centralized steward vs distributed ownership: central steward simplifies conflict resolution and visibility but introduces single-point-of-decision; mitigation: a small rotating panel of 3 stewards.

Dependencies: ENG-19834 (runtime incident SLAs), PM-271828 (cycle buffer templates), DES-220 (developer-timecard guidance).
